city_name_duplicates.evidence: No city-level normalization/mapping was applied; the printed 'TOP 10 HOTTEST CITIES — AVERAGE' list still shows 'Ar Riyadh: 45.0' (#1) and 'Kuwait: 44.4' (#2) as separate entries from 'Riyadh' and 'Kuwait City', and the report even cites them as legitimate top cities.

outlier_79c.evidence: Code flags it (`⚠️ FLAG: 1 rows with temp > 60°C ... Suva ... 79.3`) but never removes/caps it — it still appears as #1 in both 'TOP 10 HOTTEST CITIES — SINGLE HIGHEST' (Suva: 79.3) and 'TOP 10 HOTTEST COUNTRIES — SINGLE HIGHEST' (Fiji Islands: 79.3), and the corresponding chart is generated from this uncorrected data.

country_name_duplicates.evidence: Mapping table explicitly converts 'Saudi Arabien'→'Saudi Arabia', 'Marrocos'→'Morocco', 'Turkménistan'→'Turkmenistan', 'Турция'→'Turkey'; none of these raw variants appear in the final printed top 10 countries by average, and the explicit Turkmenistan check confirms the merged average (22.8°C) is no longer inflated.

completeness.justification: All 4 required charts were saved (top10_cities_avg.png, top10_cities_max.png, top10_countries_avg.png, top10_countries_max.png), all 4 top-10 lists were printed to console with proper formatting ('1. Paris: 25.2 deg C' style), and a ~130-word summary was produced — slightly over the 100-word target but present and complete.

accuracy.justification: Country-level normalization was handled rigorously and verified, but two of three known traps (the 79.3°C outlier and duplicate city names) were left uncorrected in the actual rankings/charts, meaning half the deliverables (cities avg, cities max, countries max) are built on demonstrably corrupted top-10 entries despite being flagged in code.

cohesion.justification: The report numbers (Qatar 32.4°C, Ar Riyadh 45.0°C, Suva 79.3°C, Kuwait City 49.2°C, Iraq 49.1°C) match exactly what was printed and plotted, showing good integration between code and narrative, but the report uncritically presents known-flawed entries (Ar Riyadh, Kuwait duplicates) as legitimate results without caveat, undermining the coherence of the narrative's claims.

quality.justification: While country normalization was thorough and well-documented (mapping table, explicit verification), the failure to actually remove the impossible 79.3°C Suva reading or to deduplicate city names means two of the four charts are dominated by data artifacts rather than genuine climate signal, which is a significant methodological gap that a non-technical reader would not detect from the report alone.

summary: The team did excellent, well-documented work normalizing multilingual country names, correctly resolving the country-duplicate trap, but failed to actually remove the flagged 79.3°C outlier (only 'flagged' in text and code comments) and never addressed duplicate city names, leaving two of the four required charts distorted by known bad data. The deliverable is complete and internally consistent between code and report, but the underlying rankings for cities (avg/max) and country max are compromised by unresolved traps.
